entities.summary: Venezuela is a sovereign nation in South America, Americas. Its capital is Caracas. Official languages include Spanish. Government: Federal presidential constitutional republic (de jure authoritarian regime de facto). Population: approximately 28.3 million. Area: 916,445 km². Comprehensive index for Venezuela covering indigenous peoples (Carib, Arawak, Timoto-Cuica), Columbus 1498 (first mainland), Spanish colonization, Simón Bolívar (El Libertador, birthplace Caracas, liberated 5 countries), independence 1811 (first Spanish American colony to declare), Gran Colombia 1819-30 (collapsed), Federal War 1859-63, caudillo period, Gómez dictatorship 1908-35 (27 years), oil discovery 1914 (transformed economy, 'devil's excrement'), Punto Fijo Pact 1958 (AD/COPEI alternation), Caracazo 1989 (neoliberal riots, 3,000+ killed), Hugo Chávez (1992 coup attempt, president 1999-2013, Bolivarian Revolution, socialism, oil redistribution), Nicolás Maduro (2013-present, authoritarian, economic collapse, hyperinflation, 7.7M refugees, disputed elections), and humanitarian crisis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Venezuela's independence in 1811 marked the first time a Spanish American colony declared its freedom, influencing subsequent movements for independence across the continent. The country's oil discovery in 1914 transformed its economy and had significant regional implications.
